market_sizing.target_buyer: Owner-operator (most shops are 1-5 staff family/founder-led businesses). Production manager or shop foreman co-signs at 6+ staff. NOT a brand buyer — the shop, not the apparel brand. Two sub-personas: (1) custom-decoration shop (screen print + embroidery + DTG, B2B orders for clubs/teams/corporates), (2) small cut-and-sew manufacturer making own-label garments or contract-manufacturing for AU fashion brands.
market_sizing.business_count_au: Custom decoration shops: ~800-1,500 AU. Cut-and-sew manufacturers: ~200-400 AU (most onshore manufacturing went offshore 2000-2015). Combined addressable: ~1,000-1,800. AU apparel manufacturing is small but stable. [uncertain]
market_sizing.business_count_secondary: US: ~15,000-25,000 custom decoration shops; ~3,000-5,000 cut-and-sew. UK: ~2,000-4,000 combined. NZ: ~150-300. CA: ~1,500-2,500. [uncertain]
market_sizing.typical_size: 2-12 employees. Revenue AU$200K-$3M. Cut-and-sew smaller and more capital-constrained than decoration shops.
market_sizing.growth_trend: AU cut-and-sew flat-to-slight-growth (re-shoring narrative + sustainability premium). Decoration shops 2-4% CAGR driven by team/club/corporate uniform demand. Not a fast-growing segment — solid but late-majority buyer behaviour.

fit_and_timing.addressable_window: now (cut-and-sew); decoration shops have a different buying job (order management + quoting + artwork approval) which is NOT Manuva's core wedge — they need Printavo/DecoNetwork/YoPrint.
fit_and_timing.roadmap_dependency: Lot tracking (shipped) less critical here. Xero (roadmap) important. Shopify integration shipped. NOT roadmap-gated.
fit_and_timing.typical_tier: Growth ($249) for serious cut-and-sew. Starter ($99) for smaller. Decoration shops would mostly need a Printavo competitor, not Manuva — wrong fit.
fit_and_timing.regulatory_burden: 1 — minimal. AS/NZS labelling, ethical-sourcing claims if marketed. No FSANZ/TGA/AICIS.

economics.incumbent_pricing: Decoration shops: DecoNetwork (QLD-based, AU-native, ~AU$200-500/mo), Printavo (US$95-245/mo), ShopVOX (US$129-499/mo), YoPrint (US$59-199/mo), Teesom (free tier). Cut-and-sew manufacturers: spreadsheets ~60%, Katana ~15%, Cin7 ~10%, MRPeasy ~5%, Unleashed ~5%. Big mismatch between needs and Manuva for decoration shops (different problem).
economics.willingness_to_pay_aud: Cut-and-sew: AU$149-$249/mo realistic — late-majority buyers, lower WTP. Decoration shops: not Manuva target (different problem).
economics.expansion_revenue_potential: 2 — limited upside. Cut-and-sew shops grow slowly; few expand into multi-channel selling that drives tier upgrades.
economics.churn_risk: 3 — shops do go under (margin pressure from offshore), but established 5+ year shops are very sticky.
economics.cac_estimate_aud: Cash CAC AU$200-500 (less community-driven; outbound + trade shows). Founder-time CAC ~12-18 hours × AU$150 = AU$1,800-2,700. Total ~AU$2,000-3,200. HIGHEST CAC of the Tier-A segments.
economics.ltv_cac_ratio: ~1.5-2.2:1 — POOR. Does not clear the 3:1 bar.
economics.wholesale_b2b_mix: 80-100% B2B for decoration shops; 60-90% B2B for cut-and-sew (contract manufacturing). D2C share low.

where_they_live.primary_channels: FB groups: 'Australian Screen Printers' (~3-5K [uncertain]), 'Aussie Apparel Manufacturing' (~2-4K [uncertain]). Reddit r/screenprinting (~80K global). Instagram less central. Trade shows the dominant channel. LinkedIn weak — this cohort doesn't use it heavily.
where_they_live.directories_communities: TCF Australia (Textile, Clothing and Footwear industry association). Australian Fashion Council. Council of Textile and Fashion Industries of Australia (TFIA). Print22 / Pacprint trade events. DecoNetwork community (their AU customer base). AS Colour, Gildan AU, JB's Wear — supplier-led communities. Australian Made.
where_they_live.industry_facebook_group_size: ~10,000-20,000 combined across AU apparel manufacturing + decoration FB groups [uncertain]
where_they_live.podcasts_voices: 1) PrintHustlers / Printavo podcast (US). 2) DecoNetwork blog. 3) The Apparel News (US trade). 4) Apparel Magazine AU. 5) ImpressMagazine.com.au (printing industry).
where_they_live.events_trade_shows: PacPrint (biennial, Melbourne, ~10K attendees, AU$8-25K exhibitor). Print22 (biennial). PrintEx. Reed Gift Fairs (some apparel exhibitors). Australian Fashion Week (more for brands than mfrs). TCF industry breakfasts.
where_they_live.search_keywords: 'cut and sew software Australia', 'apparel manufacturing software AU', 'screen print job tracking software', 'Printavo alternative Australia', 'DecoNetwork alternative', 'garment manufacturing inventory software', 'fabric BOM software apparel', 'Katana alternative apparel', 'small clothing factory software AU', 'embroidery shop software'

outreach_fit.cold_outbound_feasibility: 3 — shops have business numbers and email visible; cold email works moderately. Phone better than other segments (older buyers). LinkedIn weak.
outreach_fit.inbound_content_fit: 3 — late-majority buyers don't read SaaS content heavily; trade pubs better than blog SEO.
outreach_fit.founder_market_fit_proxy: 2 — this segment trusts industry-incumbent vendors (DecoNetwork is QLD-headquartered with local team — strong moat). Solo founder without apparel-industry credentials starts at disadvantage.
outreach_fit.case_study_acquisition_cost: Hard — first 3 reference customers will require trade show attendance + direct site visits. 5+ customers in 6 months is unlikely without high founder time investment.

foot_in_door_fit.trial_to_paid_benchmark: Lower than other segments. Opt-in 5-8%, CC-required 22-28%, paid pilot 35-45%. Late-majority buyers don't self-serve. They demo, then think for 3 months, then buy.
foot_in_door_fit.recommended_foot_in_door_motion: DE-PRIORITISE for the first 12 months. If pursued: Phase 3 (months 9-12+), founder-led + paid pilot (AU$249 × 3 months credited) targeting cut-and-sew manufacturers (NOT decoration shops — wrong fit). Anchor outreach through TCF Australia + Australian Fashion Council. Don't run a self-serve trial — segment doesn't self-serve. Decoration shops should be considered NOT-Manuva-ICP (DecoNetwork's home turf, different job).
foot_in_door_fit.rollout_phase: Phase 3+ (months 9-12+) — only if Phase 1 segments under-deliver

competitive_context.current_dominant_tool: Decoration shops: DecoNetwork ~40-50% (AU-headquartered moat), Printavo ~20%, ShopVOX ~10%, spreadsheets ~20%. Cut-and-sew: spreadsheets ~60%, Katana ~15%, Cin7 ~10%, MRPeasy ~5%, custom ERP ~10%.
competitive_context.switching_pain: 4 — decoration shops have complex order/quote/artwork-approval workflows; cut-and-sew has style/SKU hierarchies (size × color × fit) that are non-trivial to migrate.
competitive_context.competitor_gaps_for_this_segment: Cut-and-sew: Katana per-seat painful, weak AU Xero integration, no fabric-roll / cut-plan tracking. Cin7 too heavy. Spreadsheets: no BOM. Manuva wedge for cut-and-sew: flat AU-priced + multi-level BOM (fabric + trims + labels) + production-order workflow. But Manuva does NOT have apparel-specific size/colour matrix BOMs OR fabric cut-plan optimisation — these are real gaps that would limit fit to simpler garment shops.
competitive_context.user_satisfaction_signals: DecoNetwork has strong AU loyalty (QLD-based, local support). Printavo G2 reviews positive but US-centric. Cut-and-sew complaints on Katana focus on per-seat + weak apparel-specific features. r/screenprinting threads mention DecoNetwork as the 'aussie default' for decoration.
competitive_context.competitor_concentration: Decoration: concentrated around DecoNetwork (AU). Cut-and-sew: fragmented around spreadsheets + Katana.
competitive_context.integration_dependency_list: Must-have: Xero (roadmap — critical), Shopify (if brand-owned), QuickBooks. Custom integrations to AS Colour / JB's Wear / Gildan AU supplier catalogues are DecoNetwork's moat and a significant Manuva gap. Sublimation / DTG printer integration not in scope.

partner_channels.industry_association_sponsorship: TCF Australia / TFIA — annual sponsorship AU$2-5K. Australian Fashion Council — sponsorship AU$3-8K. PacPrint / Print22 booth AU$8-25K (defer indefinitely). Apparel Magazine AU advertorial AU$2-4K. ImpressMagazine.com.au — print-industry trade pub. Most efficient partner play: small co-marketing with AS Colour / JB's Wear (blank apparel suppliers) — they have downstream customer lists.

profitability_math.realistic_12mo_customer_count_solo: 3-8 paying customers by month 12 IF pursued. Conservative: 2. Optimistic: 12. Lowest expected volume of any Tier-A segment for the effort required.
profitability_math.realistic_12mo_mrr_contribution_aud: AU$550-1,500 MRR at AU$185 ARPU (~5 customers midpoint). Does not move the AU$3-5K MRR needle.
profitability_math.path_to_first_3k_5k_mrr_aud: This segment cannot independently deliver AU$3-5K MRR in 12 months under solo-founder constraints. Realistic 12-month contribution ~AU$1K MRR. Recommend SKIP for Phase 1 entirely. If revisited in Phase 3: TCF Australia partnership + 1-2 anchor cut-and-sew mfr reference customers + Xero ProAdvisor referrals are the only viable channels.
profitability_math.customers_needed_for_1m_arr_aud: ~450 customers at AU$185 ARPU. Unreachable without a dedicated apparel-vertical product investment (size/colour matrix BOMs + cut-plan).
profitability_math.solo_founder_bandwidth_fit: 2 — long sales cycles (60-120 days), high-touch onboarding, no community absorption of support. Bandwidth ROI is poor.
profitability_math.gross_margin_sensitivity: Medium-High — onboarding burden + Xero/QB mapping + custom supplier catalogues will erode year-1 margin to ~65-70%.
profitability_math.priority_ranking: 5 — LOWEST of the Tier-A segments. Recommend DEPRIORITISE. Three reasons: (1) DecoNetwork's AU-incumbent moat blocks the decoration sub-segment entirely (not Manuva's job anyway). (2) Cut-and-sew manufacturers need apparel-specific BOM features (size × colour matrix, cut plans) that Manuva doesn't have. (3) CAC/LTV doesn't clear 3:1. Skip for first 12 months; revisit only if Phase 1-2 segments underperform.
profitability_math.risks_and_notes: Risks/notes: (1) Manuva's hypothesis that 'Printavo is US-centric/dated; AU reach weak' is partially wrong — DecoNetwork is QLD-headquartered with local moat; that wedge does not exist. (2) Cut-and-sew sub-segment is more addressable than decoration but still requires product investment (size/colour matrix). (3) If the founder DOES want to test this segment cheaply, target 5-10 sub-AU$1M cut-and-sew mfrs via cold email + Xero ProAdvisor referrals — burn ~30 hours and decide. (4) Decoration shops should be explicitly OUT-OF-ICP messaging — don't waste demos on them. (5) Re-evaluate post-launch when Xero/MYOB/QB are shipped: that may unlock the cohort somewhat.
